title: Recording: Listen To What The Man Said by Wings | 1975
content:
Sea-Saint Recording Studio, New Orleans
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Alan O’Duffy, Ken Laxton, Roberta Grace

Wings continued work on the Venus And Mars song ‘Listen To What The Man Said’ on 21 February 1975.

This was Wings’ final recording session at Allen Toussaint’s Sea-Saint Recording Studio in New Orleans, where Wings had been working since 20 January.

The overdubs included electric guitar by Paul McCartney and Denny Laine. They were then joined by Dave Mason, whom Wings had seen perform the previous evening. Mason was enlisted to contribute additional electric guitar.

I was playing a show at the Warehouse in New Orleans, and Jimmy McCulloch and a couple of the guys came over the night of the show. And I had a day off the next day, and they were like, ‘Well, come down to the studio.’ So I just went down there and they were working on this tune and Paul was like, ‘Hey, grab a guitar – here, you see this lick – dum-dum-dum, dum-dum, dum-dum-dum,’ he said. ‘We’re just gonna play that.’ And I’m like, ‘Okay, we’re just gonna play the same lick?’ And I just threw in this little harmony on the last few notes of the lick, and he was like, ‘Oh… wait a minute… no, no, no. Okay, play it again.’ And then he said, ‘Oh, yeah, that’s cool, I like that.’ So that was my contribution.
Dave Mason, Facebook, 5 February 2021
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

After the recording, Wings and Mason had a jam session, filling two tape reels. They also began work on a new song, known as ‘The Crawl Of The Wild’.
